expansion_contract.boundary_row: enforces no parcel coverage, measured-speed or accuracy promotion from contextual evidence

guard_streams.write_limit: Checker outputs are postcode or area availability indicators; they do not prove maintenance state, a live orderable service, or measured performance at one parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the checker page on 17 August 2022.
The page was last updated on 25 June 2025.
The mobile checker shows coverage by provider after postcode entry.
The broadband checker reports standard, superfast and ultrafast availability.
Results can be viewed as interactive maps.
The checker can be viewed in Welsh.
Ofcom provides separate mobile and broadband FAQ routes.
Fixed-broadband and mobile datasets are available to developers through APIs.
Ofcom states that the checker cannot report maintenance or known local faults.
The page points users below 10 Mbit/s download speed to possible broadband USO eligibility.

guard_streams.source: Investigation into Virgin Media’s compliance with rules relating to vulnerable consumers and access to emergency organisations
guard_streams.write_limit: Enforcement findings on vulnerable-customer treatment and emergency-call continuity are compliance evidence, not broadband coverage or parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom opened the investigation on 12 December 2023.
The investigated company was VMED O2 UK trading as Virgin Media.
The investigation covered uninterrupted access to emergency organisations and treatment of vulnerable consumers.
The listed legal provisions were General Conditions A3.2, C5.2 and C5.3.
Ofcom issued a Confirmation Decision on 1 December 2025.
The Confirmation Decision was issued under section 96C of the Communications Act 2003.
Ofcom found a contravention of General Condition C5.2.
The recorded contravention period ran from August 2022 to December 2023.
A non-confidential Confirmation Decision was published on 19 January 2026.
The official case record shows closure on 19 January 2026.
